issues.spec_citation: FHIRPath Normative Release Section 6.2 Comparison and Section 6.1 DateTime timezone comparison discussion
issues.evidence: Fresh FP-14 EXPLORER probe found native/fallback divergence for one-sided DateTime timezone comparisons. Reproducer: `@2017-11-05T01:30:00.0-04:00 >= @2017-11-05T01:30:00.0` returned true in native C++ but false in forced Python fallback; the reverse `<` case returned false in native but true in fallback. Section 6.2 requires DateTime comparisons to respect timezone offsets, and Section 6.1 states behavior for DateTime values without offsets is implementation policy; the two DuckDB backends should not expose different policies.
issues.root_cause: Python fallback `FP_TimeBase.compare()` stripped a one-sided timezone for normalized field comparison, but equal-precision comparisons then used `_getDateTimeInt()` on the original DateTime objects, reintroducing the offset and diverging from native C++ raw shared-precision policy.
issues.resolution: When exactly one DateTime operand has a timezone offset, the fallback now compares the already-normalized shared-precision field lists directly instead of using `_getDateTimeInt()` on the original objects. Added native-vs-forced-fallback parity coverage for `<`, `>`, `<=`, and `>=`.
